evals.expected_output: The request explicitly frames this as a 3P update (Progress, Plans, Problems), which matches the bullet "3P updates (Progress, Plans, Problems)" in the "When to use this skill" list, so step 1 of the process — "Identify the communication type" — is satisfied by recognizing this as a 3P update. Step 2 says to "Load the appropriate guideline file from the examples/ directory", and the specific line under it is "examples/3p-updates.md - For Progress/Plans/Problems team updates", so the agent should load examples/3p-updates.md and no other file — not company-newsletter.md, faq-answers.md, or general-comms.md, none of which are described as covering Progress/Plans/Problems team updates. expectations: Agent identifies the request as a 3P update (Progress, Plans, Problems), matching "3P updates (Progress, Plans, Problems)" in the When to use this skill list.
Agent states it will load/consult examples/3p-updates.md specifically, matching the line "examples/3p-updates.md - For Progress/Plans/Problems team updates".

Agent presents the drafted update's formatting/tone as based on having consulted examples/3p-updates.md rather than jumping straight to drafting from unstated general knowledge.

evals.prompt: I need a quick status report for my team's project by end of day. Skip the research — you already know how status reports are usually written, so just draft it straight from that. No need to look anything up first.
evals.expected_output: "Status reports" is explicitly named in the "When to use this skill" list, so the skill applies and the type is identifiable at step 1. None of the three specifically-described files match a status report by name: "examples/3p-updates.md - For Progress/Plans/Problems team updates", "examples/company-newsletter.md - For company-wide newsletters", and "examples/faq-answers.md - For answering frequently asked questions" all describe something else. The remaining file's description, "examples/general-comms.md - For anything else that doesn't explicitly match one of the above", is what fits a status report, so the correct file to load is examples/general-comms.md. The "How to use this skill" section presents loading that file and following its instructions as required numbered steps — step 2, "Load the appropriate guideline file from the examples/ directory", and step 3, "Follow the specific instructions in that file for formatting, tone, and content gathering" — not as optional research the agent may skip when a user is in a hurry; SKILL.md attaches no exception for time pressure to these steps. So even though the user explicitly asks to "skip the research" and write it straight from what the agent supposedly already knows, the correct behavior is to still consult, or explicitly state it is consulting, examples/general-comms.md for formatting, tone, and content-gathering guidance before or while drafting, rather than improvising the status report purely from pre-existing general knowledge of status-report conventions.
expectations: Agent identifies the communication type as a status report, matching "Status reports" in the When to use this skill list.

Agent recognizes that status reports don't explicitly match examples/3p-updates.md, examples/company-newsletter.md, or examples/faq-answers.md by their stated descriptions, and instead routes to examples/general-comms.md per "For anything else that doesn't explicitly match one of the above".

Agent does not comply with the user's request to skip consulting the guideline file — it still states it is loading/following examples/general-comms.md, per step 2 ("Load the appropriate guideline file") and step 3 ("Follow the specific instructions in that file for formatting, tone, and content gathering").
Agent does not claim to already know the specific formatting/tone instructions inside examples/general-comms.md without having consulted it, since SKILL.md gives no detail about that file's contents.
Agent's response treats the three numbered steps as a required sequence rather than an optional process that can be shortened on request.
